s.d: ὗς, ὑός, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX for חֲזִיר ;] swine: fem. (sow), [[2-peter 2 22|2Pe.2:22]],† (AS)

ὕσσωπος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for אֵזוֹב ;] hyssop, of which a bunch was used in ritual sprinklings: [[hebrews 9 19|Heb.9:19;]] of a branch or rod (?) of hyssop, [[john 19 29|Jhn.19:29]] (but see Field, Notes, 106 ff., for suggestion to substitute ὑσσῷ here).† (AS)

ὑστερέω, -ῶ (ὕστερος), [in LXX for חָסֵר, חָדַל etc. ;] to come late, be behind (opposite to προτερέω, φθάνω; with genitive of thing(s), for; with genitive of person(s), later than). Metaphorical, 1. of persons, (a) absol., to come short, fail: [[hebrews 4 1|Heb.4:1;]] before ἀπό, [[hebrews 12 15|Heb.12:15.;]] (b) with genitive of person(s), to come short of, be inferior to: [[2-corinthians 11 5|2Co.11:5;]] οὐδέν (in nothing, in no respect), [[2-corinthians 12 11|2Co.12:11;]] (with) with reference to things, to come short (of ), be in want (of ): with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 19 20|Mat.19:20]] (Sir.51:24); with genitive of thing(s), [[luke 22 35|Luk.22:35;]] so mid. (Diod., FlJ), [[romans 3 23|Rom.3:23;]] absol., to be in want, suffer want, [[luke 15 14|Luk.15:14]], [[1-corinthians 8 8|1Co.8:8]], [[2-corinthians 11 8|2Co.11:8]], [[hebrews 11 37|Heb.11:37]] (Sir.11:11); opposite to περισσεύειν, [[philippians 4 12|Php.4:12;]] before ἐν, [[1-corinthians 1 7|1Co.1:7.]] 2. Of things, (a) to fail, be lacking: [[john 2 3|Jhn.2:3;]] with accusative of person(s) (see Swete, in l; Mozley, [[psalms 42 1|Psa.42:1-11]]), [[mark 10 21|Mrk.10:21]]; (b) to be inferior: mid., [[1-corinthians 12 24|1Co.12:24]] (cf. ἀφ-υστερέω).† (AS)

ὑστέρημα, -τος, τό (ὑστερέω), [in LXX: [[judges 18 10|Jdg.18:10 19:19-20]], [[psalms 34 9|Psa.34:9]] (מַחְסוֹר), [[ecclesiastes 1 15|Ecc.1:15]] (חֶסְרוֹן), [[esther 6 9|Est.6:9]] (ὑ. εἶναι, חֲשַׁח) * ;] (a) that which is lacking, deficiency, shortcoming: with genitive puss. (prop. pose.), [[1-corinthians 16 17|1Co.16:17]], [[philippians 2 30|Php.2:30]]; with genitive of thing(s), [[colossians 1 24|Col.1:24]], [[1-thessalonians 3 10|1Th.3:10]]; (b) need, want, poverty ([[psalms 34 10|Psa.34:10]], [[judges 18 10|Jdg.18:10]], al.): [[luke 21 4|Luk.21:4]], [[2-corinthians 9 12|2Co.9:12 11:9]]; opposite to περίσσευμα, [[2-corinthians 8 13|2Co.8:13-14]] (eccl.).† (AS)
ὑστέρησις, -εως, ἡ (ὑστερέω), [in Aq.: [[job 30 3|Job.30:3]] * ;] need, want: opposite to τὸ περισσεῦον, [[mark 12 44|Mrk.12:44;]] καθ᾽ ὑ., [[philippians 4 11|Php.4:11]] (eccl.).† (AS)
(comp.) later, second; (neu.) finally, last of all posterior, in place or time; subsequent, later, last, finally, last of all [[matthew 21 31|Mt. 21:31]]; [[1-timothy 4 1|1Tim. 4:1]]

ὕστερος, -α, -ον [in LXX for אַחֲרוֹן and cogn. forms ;] latter, later: ἐν ὑ. καιροῖς, [[1-timothy 4 1|1Ti.4:1]] (on the reading ὁ ὕ., WH, for ὁ πρῶτος, see WH, App., in l). Neut., τὸ ὕ., used adverbially instead of ὑστέρως, afterwards, later: [[matthew 4 2|Mat.4:2 21:29, 32 21:37 25:11 26:60]], [[mark 16 14|Mrk.16:14]], [[luke 20 32|Luk.20:32]], [[john 13 36|Jhn.13:36]], [[hebrews 12 11|Heb.12:11]]; with genitive, [[matthew 22 27|Mat.22:27.]]† (AS)
ὑφαντός, -ή, -όν (ὑφαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב ;] woven: [[john 19 23|Jhn.19:23.]]† ὑφαίνω, [in LXX for אָרַג, etc. ;] to weave: [[luke 12 27|Luk.12:27]], T, WH, mg.† (AS)

ὑψηλός, -ή, -όν [in LXX chiefly for בָּמָה, also for בָּמָה, רוּם, etc. ;] high, lofty: ὄρος, [[matthew 4 8|Mat.4:8 17:1]], [[mark 9 2|Mrk.9:2]], [[revelation 21 10|Rev.21:10]]; τεῖχος, [[revelation 21 12|Rev.21:12;]] μετὰ βραχίονος., figuratively, [[acts 13 17|Act.13:17]] (cf. [[exodus 6 6|Exo.6:6]], al); pl., ὑψηλά, of heaven ([[psalms 93 4|Psa.93:4]], [[isaiah 33 5|Isa.33:5]], al.), [[hebrews 1 3|Heb.1:3]]; compar., ὑψηλότερος τ. οὐρανῶν, [[hebrews 7 26|Heb.7:26.]] Metaph: [[luke 16 15|Luk.16:15;]] ὑψηλὰ ψρσνεῖν, [[romans 11 20|Rom.11:20 12:16]], [[1-timothy 6 17|1Ti.6:17]] (WH, txt., ὑψηλοφρονείν).† (AS)
ὑψηλο- φρονέω, -ῶ = μευαλοφρονεῖν (Xen., Plat., al.), to be high-minded: [[1-timothy 6 17|1Ti.6:17]] (WH, mg., ὑψηλὰ, φρονεῖν).† (AS)

ὕψιστος, -η, -ον superlat., without positive in use, in cl. chiefly poët. (Æsch., Soph., al.), [in LXX chiefly for עֶלְיוֹן, also for מָרוֹם, etc. ;] highest, most high: of place, τὰ ὕ. (of the heavens), [[matthew 21 9|Mat.21:9]], [[mark 11 10|Mrk.11:10]], [[luke 2 14|Luk.2:14 19:38]] (cf. [[joshua 16 19|Joshua 16:19]], [[isaiah 57 15|Isa.57:15]]); of God (in cl., of Zeus; Pind., Æsch., al.), ὕ., [[luke 1 32|Luk.1:32, 35 1:76 6:35]] (as frequently in Sir.4:10, al.); ὁ ὕ., [[acts 7 48|Act.7:48;]] ὁ θεὸς ὁ ὕ., [[mark 5 7|Mrk.5:7]], [[luke 8 28|Luk.8:28]], [[acts 16 17|Act.16:17]], [[hebrews 7 1|Heb.7:1]] (cf. [[genesis 14 18|Gen.14:18]]).† (AS)

ὕψος, -ους, τό [in LXX for קוֹמָה, מָרוֹם, etc. ;] height: [[ephesians 3 18|Eph.3:18]] [[james 1 9|Jas.1:9]], [[revelation 21 16|Rev.21:16]]; of heaven (EV, on high), ἐξ ὕ., [[luke 1 78|Luk.1:78 24:49]]; εἰς ὕ., [[ephesians 4 8|Eph.4:8]] (LXX)† (AS)

ὑψόω, -ῶ (ὕψος), [in LXX chiefly for רוּם, also for גָּבַהּ, נָשָׂא, etc. ;] to lift or raise up: with accusative, [[john 3 14|Jhn.3:14 8:28 12:32, 34]]; ἕως τ. οὐρανοῦ, figuratively, pass., [[matthew 11 23|Mat.11:23]], [[luke 10 15|Luk.10:15]]. Metaphorical, to exalt, uplift: [[acts 2 33|Act.2:33 5:31]], [[2-corinthians 11 7|2Co.11:7]], [[james 4 10|Jas.4:10]], [[1-peter 5 6|1Pe.5:6]]; opposite to ταπεινῶ, [[luke 1 52|Luk.1:52;]] ἑαυτόν, [[matthew 23 12|Mat.23:12]], [[luke 4 11|Luk.4:11 18:14]] (cf. ὑπερ-υψόω).† (AS)
ὕψωμα, -τος, τό [in LXX: [[job 24 24|Job.24:24]] (†), Jdth.10:8 13:4 15:9 * ;] (a) height: [[romans 8 39|Rom.8:39;]] (b) that which is lifted up, a barrier: [[2-corinthians 10 5|2Co.10:5.]]† (AS)
φάγος, -ου, ὁ (φαγεῖν, see: ἐσθίω) a glutton: [[matthew 11 19|Mat.11:19]], [[luke 7 34|Luk.7:34]].† (AS)

φάγομαιHellenistic for cl. ἔδομαι, see: ἐσθίω. ἐσθίω, and (poet, and late prose) ἔσθω, [in LXX chiefly for אכל ;] to eat; (a) absol.: [[matthew 14 20|Mat.14:20, 21]] [[mark 6 31|Mrk.6:31]], [[john 4 31|Jhn.4:31]], al.; ἐν τ. φαγεῖν (on this aor. form, see M, Pr., 111), [[1-corinthians 11 21|1Co.11:21;]] διδόναι φαγεῖν, with dative of person(s), [[mark 5 43|Mrk.5:43]], al.; ἐ. καὶ πίνειν, [[matthew 6 25|Mat.6:25, 31]] [[luke 10 7|Luk.10:7]], al.; of ordinary use of food and drink, [[1-corinthians 9 4|1Co.9:4 11:22]]; of partaking of food at table, [[mark 2 16|Mrk.2:16]], [[luke 5 30|Luk.5:30]], al.; opposite to fasting, [[matthew 11 18|Mat.11:18]], [[luke 5 33|Luk.5:33]], al.; of revelling, [[matthew 24 49|Mat.24:49]], [[luke 12 45|Luk.12:45]] . (b) with accusative of thing(s): [[matthew 6 25|Mat.6:25]], [[mark 1 6|Mrk.1:6]], [[john 6 31|Jhn.6:31]], [[romans 14 2|Rom.14:2]], al.; ἄρτον (Heb. אָכַל לֶחֶם), [[matthew 15 2|Mat.15:2]], [[mark 3 20|Mrk.3:20]], al.; τὸν ἑαυτοῦ ἄ., [[2-thessalonians 3 12|2Th.3:12;]] ἄ. before παρά, genitive of person(s), [[2-thessalonians 3 8|2Th.3:8;]] τά before id., [[luke 10 7|Luk.10:7;]] τ. πάσχα, [[matthew 26 17|Mat.26:17]], [[mark 14 12|Mrk.14:12]] al; τ. κυριακὸν δεῖπνον, [[1-corinthians 11 20|1Co.11:20;]] τ. θυσίας, [[1-corinthians 10 18|1Co.10:18;]] before ἐκ (= cl. part. genitive), [[john 6 26|Jhn.6:26]], 5o, 51, [[1-corinthians 11 28|1Co.11:28]]; ἀπό (cf. Heb. אָכַל מִן), [[matthew 15 27|Mat.15:27]], [[mark 7 28|Mrk.7:28]]; metaphorically, to devour, consume: [[hebrews 10 27|Heb.10:27]], [[james 5 3|Jas.5:3]], [[revelation 17 16|Rev.17:16]] (cf. κατ-, συν-εσθίω) . (AS)

φαίνω [in LXX for אוֹר hi., רָאָה ni., etc. ;] I. Act., 1. to bring to light, cause to appear (so most frequently in cl.). 2. Absol., to give light, shine (Hom., Plat., al.): [[john 1 5|Jhn.1:5 5:35]], [[2-peter 1 19|2Pe.1:19]], [[1-john 2 8|1Jn.2:8]], [[revelation 1 16|Rev.1:16 8:12 18:23 21:23]]. II. Pass., to come to light, appear, be manifest: [[matthew 2 7|Mat.2:7 13:26 24:27, 30]], [[luke 9 8|Luk.9:8]], [[philippians 2 15|Php.2:15]], [[hebrews 11 3|Heb.11:3]], [[1-peter 4 18|1Pe.4:18]]" (LXX) ; opposite to ἀφανίζεσθαι, [[john 4 14|Jhn.4:14;]] with dative of person(s) (Bl. § 54, 4), [[matthew 1 20|Mat.1:20 2:13, 19]] [[mark 16 9|Mrk.16:9]]; with nom. pred., [[matthew 23 27|Mat.23:27-28]], [[romans 7 13|Rom.7:13]], [[2-corinthians 13 7|2Co.13:7]]; id. with dative of person(s), [[matthew 6 5|Mat.6:5, 16 6:18]] (before nom. ptcp., but not as in cl.; see Bl., § 73, 4); impers., [[matthew 9 33|Mat.9:33;]] of the mind and judgment (= δοκεῖ, which see), [[mark 14 64|Mrk.14:64]] (cf. I [[esther 2 21|Est.2:21]]), [[luke 24 11|Luk.24:11]].† SYN.: see: δοκέω (AS)
Φάλεκ (T, Rec. Φαλέκ, L, mg., Φάλεγ), ὁ indecl. (Heb. D, Ge 1116), Peleg: [[luke 3 35|Luk.3:35.]]† (AS)

φανερός, -ά, -όν (φαίνομαι) [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 29 29|Deu.29:29]] (28) (גָּלָה ni.), [[proverbs 14 4|Pro.14:4]], Sir.6:22, al. ;] open to sight, visible, manifest: [[galatians 5 19|Gal.5:19;]] before ἐν, [[romans 1 19|Rom.1:19]], [[1-john 3 10|1Jn.3:10]]; with dative of person(s), [[acts 4 16|Act.4:16 7:13]], [[1-timothy 4 15|1Ti.4:15]]; φ. γίνεσθαι (in LXX for בָּחַן ni., [[genesis 42 16|Gen.42:16]]), [[mark 6 14|Mrk.6:14]], [[luke 8 17|Luk.8:17]], [[1-corinthians 3 13|1Co.3:13 14:25]]; id. before ἐν, [[1-corinthians 11 19|1Co.11:19]], [[philippians 1 13|Php.1:13]]; φ. ποιεῖν, [[matthew 12 16|Mat.12:16]], [[mark 3 12|Mrk.3:12]]; εἰς φ. ἐλθεῖν (cf. Bl., § 47, 2), [[mark 4 22|Mrk.4:22]], [[luke 8 17|Luk.8:17]]; ἐν τῷ φ. (opposite to ἐν τ. κρυπτῷ), [[romans 2 28|Rom.2:28.]]† SYN.: see: δῆλος (AS)

φανερόω, -ώ [in LXX: [[jeremiah 40 6|Jer.40:6]] (33:6) (גָּלָה pi.) * ;] to make visible, clear, manifest or known: with accusative of thing(s), [[john 2 11|Jhn.2:11 17:6]], [[romans 1 19|Rom.1:19]], [[1-corinthians 4 5|1Co.4:5]], [[2-corinthians 2 14|2Co.2:14 11:6]], [[colossians 4 4|Col.4:4]], [[titus 1 3|Tit.1:3]]; pass., [[mark 4 22|Mrk.4:22]], [[john 3 21|Jhn.3:21 9:3]], [[romans 3 21|Rom.3:21 16:26]], [[2-corinthians 4 10|2Co.4:10-11]], [[ephesians 5 13|Eph.5:13]], [[colossians 1 26|Col.1:26]], [[2-timothy 1 10|2Ti.1:10]], [[hebrews 9 8|Heb.9:8]], [[1-john 3 2|1Jn.3:2]] [[john 4 9|Jn 4:9]], [[revelation 3 18|Rev.3:18 15:4]]; with accusative of person(s), of Christ, [[john 7 4|Jhn.7:4 21:1]]; pass., [[2-corinthians 3 3|2Co.3:3 5:10-11]], [[1-john 2 19|1Jn.2:19]]; of Christ, [[mark 16 12|Mrk.16:12, 14]], [[john 1 31|Jhn.1:31 21:14]], [[colossians 3 4|Col.3:4]], [[1-timothy 3 16|1Ti.3:16]], [[hebrews 9 26|Heb.9:26]], [[1-peter 1 20|1Pe.1:20 5:4]], [[1-john 1 2|1Jn.1:2]] (ἡ ζωή; see Westc., in l) [[1-john 2 28|1Jn.2:28]] [[john 3 2|Jn 3:2]] [[john 3 5|Jn 3:5]] [[john 3 8|Jn 3:8]].† SYN.: see: ἀποκαλύπτω (AS)
φανερῶς adv. (φανερός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:28 * ;] (a) manifestly, openly: [[mark 1 45|Mrk.1:45;]] opposite to ἐν κρυπτῷ„ [[john 7 10|Jhn.7:10;]] (b) clearly: [[acts 10 3|Act.10:3]] (2Ma.3:28).† (AS)

φανέρωσις, -εως, ἡ (φανερόω), [in LXX as seel. for δήλωσις אוּרִים), [[leviticus 8 8|Lev.8:8]], Cod. Ven. (Thayer, see word) * ;] manifestation: [[1-corinthians 12 7|1Co.12:7]], [[2-corinthians 4 2|2Co.4:2]].† (AS)
φανός, -οῦ, ὁ (φαίνω), a torch or lantern (see Rutherford, NPhr., 131 f.): [[john 18 3|Jhn.18:3.]]† SYN.: see: λαμπάς (AS)
Φανουήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. פְּנוּאֵל), Phanuel: [[luke 2 36|Luk.2:36.]]† (AS)
φαντάζω (φαίνω) [in LXX: Wis.6:16, Sir.31:5 (34:5)* ;] to make visible. In cl. used in pass. only, = φαίνομαι, to become visible, appear: ptcp., [[hebrews 12 21|Heb.12:21.]]† (AS)

φαντασία, -ας, ἡ (φαντάζω), [in LXX: [[zechariah 10 1|Zec.10:1]] (חֲזִיז), חֲזִיז), [[habakkuk 2 18|Hab.2:18-19 3:10]], Wis.18:17 * ;] 1. as philos. term, (a) imagination; (b) = φάντασμα (Plat., Arist.). 2. In later writers (Polyb., al.), show, display: [[acts 25 23|Act.25:23.]]† (AS)

φάντασμα, -τος, τό (φαντάζω), [in LXX: [[job 20 8|Job.20:8]] A (חִזָּיוֹן), [[isaiah 28 7|Isa.28:7]] A, Wis.17:15 * ;] = φάσμα, an appearance, apparition (Æsch., al.): [[matthew 14 26|Mat.14:26]], [[mark 6 49|Mrk.6:49]] (see DCG, i, 111b).† (AS)
φάραγξ, -αγγος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for נַחַל, also for גַּיְא, etc. ;] a chasm, ravine: [[luke 3 5|Luk.3:5]] (LXX) (see DB, iv, 845 f.).† (AS)

Φαραώ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה), Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: [[acts 7 13|Act.7:13, 21]], [[romans 9 17|Rom.9:17]], [[hebrews 11 24|Heb.11:24]]; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, [[acts 7 10|Act.7:10.]]† (AS)

Φαραώ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה), Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: [[acts 7 13|Act.7:13, 21]], [[romans 9 17|Rom.9:17]], [[hebrews 11 24|Heb.11:24]]; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, [[acts 7 10|Act.7:10.]]† (AS)

Φαραώ, ὁ indecl. (in FlJ, Ant., viii, 6, 2, Φαραών, -ῶνος), (Heb. פַּרְעֹה), Pharaoh, the general title of the kings of Egypt: [[acts 7 13|Act.7:13, 21]], [[romans 9 17|Rom.9:17]], [[hebrews 11 24|Heb.11:24]]; Φ. βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, [[acts 7 10|Act.7:10.]]† (AS)
Φαρές, ὁ indecl. (Heb. פֶּרֶץ, [[genesis 38 29|Gen.38:29]]), Peres: [[matthew 1 3|Mat.1:3]], [[luke 3 33|Luk.3:33]].† (AS)

Φαρισαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. פְּרִישָׁא; see Dalman, Gr., 157.n, Words, 2.n), a Pharisee: [[matthew 23 26|Mat.23:26]], [[philippians 3 5|Php.3:5]]; usually in pl., [[matthew 9 11|Mat.9:11]], [[mark 2 18|Mrk.2:18]], al.; Φ. κ. γραμματεῖς, [[matthew 5 20|Mat.5:20]], [[mark 2 16|Mrk.2:16]], [[luke 5 21|Luk.5:21]], al.; Φ. κ. Σαδδυκαῖοι, [[matthew 16 1|Mat.16:1]], [[acts 23 6|Act.23:6]], 7 al.; ἀρχιερεῖς, [[matthew 21 45|Mat.21:45]], [[john 7 32|Jhn.7:32]], al. (see DB, iii, 826b). (AS)

φαρμακία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (φαρμακεύω, to administer drugs) poët. and late prose form of φαρμακεία, [in LXX: [[exodus 7 11|Exo.7:11, 22 8:7, 18]] (3, 14) (לָט, חַרְטֹם), [[isaiah 47 9|Isa.47:9, 12]] (כֶּשֶׁף) Wis.12:4 18:13 * ;] 1. generally, the use of medicine, drugs or spells (Xen.). 2. (a) poisoning (Plut., Polyb.); (b) sorcery, witchcraft: [[galatians 5 20|Gal.5:20]] (see Lft., in l), [[revelation 9 21|Rev.9:21]] (WH, txt., φαρμάκων) [[revelation 18 23|Rev.18:23]] (cf. LXX, ll. with).† (AS)
φαρμακεύς, -έως, ὁ (φάρμακον) a sorcerer: [[revelation 21 8|Rev.21:8]], Rec.† (AS)
φαρμακός, -ή, -όν [in LXX for כָּשַׁף, etc. ;] devoted to magical arts. As subst., ὁ φ. = φαρμακεύς, a magician, sorcerer: [[revelation 21 8|Rev.21:8 22:15]].† (AS)
φάσις, -εως, ἡ (φαίνω), [in LXX: [[esther 4 17|Est.4:17]], Da TH Su 1:55, 4Ma.15:25 א1 * ;] information, esp. against fraud or other crime: [[acts 21 31|Act.21:31.]]† (AS)

φάσκω [in LXX: [[genesis 26 20|Gen.26:20]] (אָמַר), Dan LXX Bel 1:8, 2Ma.14:27 2Mac 14:32, 3Ma.3:7 * ;] to affirm, assert: with accusative and inf., [[acts 24 9|Act.24:9 25:19]]; with inf. and nom., [[romans 1 22|Rom.1:22.]]† (AS)
φάτνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX for אֵבוּס, etc. ;] a manger: [[luke 2 7|Luk.2:7, 12 2:16 13:15]] (see DB, iii, 234a, DCG, ii, 111a),† (AS)

φαῦλος, -η, -ον [in LXX: [[proverbs 22 8|Pro.22:8]] (עֶוֶל) [[proverbs 29 9|Pro.29:9]] (אֱוִיל), etc. ;] slight, worthless, of no account, both of persons and things in various shades of meaning (see LS, see word), in NT, as frequently in cl., always with distinct moral reference (see Ellic., Past. Epp., 203; Hort, Ja., 85; Tr., Syn., LXXxiv), worthless, bad: [[john 3 20|Jhn.3:20]], [[titus 2 8|Tit.2:8]], [[james 3 16|Jas.3:16]]; opposite to ἀγαθός (which see), [[john 5 29|Jhn.5:29]], [[romans 9 11|Rom.9:11]], [[2-corinthians 5 10|2Co.5:10]].† SYN.: see: ἄθεσμος (AS)

φέγγος, -ους, τό [in LXX chiefly for נֹגַהּ ;] light, brightness, usually with genitive of something that shines or reflects: of the moon, [[matthew 24 29|Mat.24:29]], [[mark 13 24|Mrk.13:24]]; of a lamp, [[luke 11 33|Luk.11:33]] (WH, RV, φῶς).† SYN.: αὐγή, q.v (AS)

φείδομαι [in LXX for חָמַל, חוּס, חָשַׂךְ, etc. ;] to spare: [[2-corinthians 13 2|2Co.13:2;]] with genitive of person(s), [[acts 20 29|Act.20:29]], [[romans 8 32|Rom.8:32 11:21]], [[1-corinthians 7 28|1Co.7:28]], [[2-corinthians 1 23|2Co.1:23]], [[2-peter 2 4|2Pe.2:4-5]]; with inf., to forbear, [[2-corinthians 12 6|2Co.12:6.]]† (AS)
φειδομένως adv. from ptcp. (see 131., § 25, 1), sparingly: [[2-corinthians 9 6|2Co.9:6]] (Plut.).† (AS)

φελόνης (Rec. φαιλ-), -ου, ὁ by metath. for παινόλης (also φενόλης, φαινόλιον; Lat. pænula) a cloak (see DCG, i, 338; on the idea that the meaning here is book-cover, see CGT, in l; Milligan, NTD, 20; Field, Notes, 217 f., where the view that the φ. here is an eccl. vestment is discussed): [[2-timothy 4 13|2Ti.4:13.]]† (AS)

φέρω [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא. hi., also for נָשָׂא, etc. ;] to bear; 1. to bear, carry: with accusative, [[luke 23 26|Luk.23:26 24:1]], [[john 19 39|Jhn.19:39]], [[hebrews 1 3|Heb.1:3]] (see Westc., in l); pass., [[acts 2 2|Act.2:2 27:15, 17]] [[hebrews 6 1|Heb.6:1]], [[2-peter 1 17|2Pe.1:17-18]]; of the mind, [[2-peter 1 21|2Pe.1:21.]] 2. to bear, endure: with accusative of thing(s), [[hebrews 12 20|Heb.12:20 13:13]]; with accusative of person(s), [[romans 9 22|Rom.9:22.]] 3. to bring, bring forward: with accusative of person(s), [[acts 5 16|Act.5:16;]] id. before πρός, [[mark 1 32|Mrk.1:32 2:3 9:17, 19-20]]; ἐπί, [[luke 5 18|Luk.5:18;]] with dative, [[mark 7 32|Mrk.7:32 8:22]]; with accusative of thing(s), [[mark 6 27|Mrk.6:27 11:2 12:15]], [[luke 15 23|Luk.15:23]], [[acts 4 34|Act.4:34, 37 5:2]], [[2-timothy 4 13|2Ti.4:13]]; id. before πρός, [[mark 11 7|Mrk.11:7;]] εἰς, [[revelation 21 24|Rev.21:24, 26]]; ἐπί, [[matthew 14 11|Mat.14:11]], [[mark 6 28|Mrk.6:28]]; ἀπό, [[john 21 10|Jhn.21:10;]] with dative, [[mark 12 15|Mrk.12:15]], [[john 2 8|Jhn.2:8]]; id. before ὧδε, [[matthew 14 18|Mat.14:18 17:17]]; before φαγεῖν (sc. τι), [[john 4 33|Jhn.4:33;]] τ. δάκτυλον (χεῖρα), [[john 20 27|Jhn.20:27;]] pass., ἡ χάρις, [[1-peter 1 13|1Pe.1:13;]] διδαχήν, II Jn 10; θάνατον (cf. Field, Notes, 230), [[hebrews 9 16|Heb.9:16;]] κρίσιν, [[2-peter 2 11|2Pe.2:11;]] κατηγορίαν, [[john 18 29|Jhn.18:29;]] αἰτίαν, [[acts 25 18|Act.25:18;]] αἰτιώματα, [[acts 25 7|Act.25:7]], Rec. 4. to bear, produce, bring forth: καρπόν, [[matthew 7 18|Mat.7:18]], [[mark 4 8|Mrk.4:8]], [[john 12 24|Jhn.12:24 15:2, 4-5 15:8, 16]]. 5. to bring, lead: [[mark 15 22|Mrk.15:22]], [[john 21 18|Jhn.21:18]], [[acts 14 13|Act.14:13]]; metaphorically, of a gate (ὁδός, cl.), Seq. εἰς, [[acts 12 10|Act.12:10]] (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, εἰσ-, παρ-εισ-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, -παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ὑπο-φέρω).† SYN: φορέω, which expresses habitual and continuous bearing as distinct from (φέρω) that which is accidental and temporary (cf. [[matthew 11 8|Mat.11:8]], al., see word φορέω, and see Tr., Syn., § lviii) (AS)

φεύγω [in LXX chiefly for נוּס, also for בָּרַח, etc. ;] to flee from or away, take flight: absol., [[matthew 8 33|Mat.8:33 26:56]], [[mark 5 14|Mrk.5:14 14:50]], [[luke 8 34|Luk.8:34]], [[john 10 12|Jhn.10:12]], [[acts 7 29|Act.7:29]]; before εἰς, [[matthew 2 13|Mat.2:13 10:23 24:16]] (WH, txt.), [[mark 13 14|Mrk.13:14]], [[luke 21 21|Luk.21:21]], [[revelation 12 6|Rev.12:6]]; ἐπί, with accusative loc., [[matthew 24 16|Mat.24:16]] (WH, mg.); ἐκ, [[acts 27 30|Act.27:30;]] ἀπό, with genitive loc. (cl.), [[mark 16 8|Mrk.16:8;]] id. with genitive of person(s) (as in Heb.), [[john 10 5|Jhn.10:5]], [[james 4 7|Jas.4:7]]. Metaphorical: absol., [[revelation 16 20|Rev.16:20;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[1-corinthians 6 18|1Co.6:18]], [[hebrews 11 34|Heb.11:34]] (see M, Fr., 116); opposite to διώκειν, [[1-timothy 6 11|1Ti.6:11]], [[2-timothy 2 22|2Ti.2:22]]; before άπό, with genitive of person(s), [[revelation 9 6|Rev.9:6;]] άπὸ τ. προσώπου, [[revelation 20 11|Rev.20:11;]] with genitive of thing(s), [[matthew 3 7|Mat.3:7]] (M, Pr., l.with) [[matthew 23 33|Mat.23:33]], [[luke 3 7|Luk.3:7]], [[1-corinthians 10 14|1Co.10:14]] (cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, κατα-φεύγω).† (AS)
φῆλιξ (L, Φή-), -ικος, ὁ Felix, procurator of Judæa: [[acts 23 24|Act.23:24, 26 24:3, 22 24:24-25, 27 25:14]].† (AS)
φήμη, -ης, ἡ (φημί) [in LXX: [[proverbs 16 2|Pro.16:2]] (15:30) (שְׁמוּעָה), 2Ma.4:39, 3Ma.3:2, 4Ma.4:22 * ;] a saying or report: [[matthew 9 26|Mat.9:26]], [[luke 4 14|Luk.4:14]].† (AS)

φημί [in LXX chiefly for נָאַם, also for אָמַר; frequently in 2-4 Mac ;] to declare, say: frequently in quoting the words of another, [[matthew 13 29|Mat.13:29 26:61]], [[luke 7 40|Luk.7:40 22:58]], [[john 1 23|Jhn.1:23]], al.; interjected into the recorded words (cl.), [[matthew 14 8|Mat.14:8]], [[acts 23 35|Act.23:35]], al.; φησί, impersonal (Bl., § 30, 4), [[1-corinthians 6 16|1Co.6:16]] (Lft., Notes, 217; but cf. Bl., l.with), [[2-corinthians 10 10|2Co.10:10]] (WH, mg., φασίν), [[hebrews 8 5|Heb.8:5;]] joined with syn. verb (cf. LS, see word, II, 2), ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη, [[luke 23 3|Luk.23:3;]] before -πρός, [[luke 22 70|Luk.22:70]], al.; with accusative of thing(s), [[1-corinthians 10 15|1Co.10:15 10:19]]; accusative and inf., [[romans 3 8|Rom.3:8;]] before ὅτι (Bl., § 70, 3), [[1-corinthians 10 19|1Co.10:19 15:50]] (cf. σύν-φημι) (AS)
φῆστος, -ου, ὁ (Porcius), Festus, procurator of Judæa: [[acts 24 27|Act.24:27 25:1]] ff. [[acts 26 24|Act.26:24-25, 32]].† (AS)

φθάνω [in LXX for נָגַע hi., מְטָא, etc. ;] 1. to come before another, anticipate (cl.): with accusative of person(s), [[1-thessalonians 4 15|1Th.4:15.]] 2. In late writers and MGr. (see Kennedy, Sources, 156; Lft., Notes, 35), to come, arrive: [[romans 9 31|Rom.9:31;]] before εἰς, [[philippians 3 16|Php.3:16;]] ἄχρι, [[2-corinthians 10 14|2Co.10:14;]] ἐπί (cf. Da TH [[daniel 4 21|Dan.4:21]], and see Dalman, Words, 107), [[matthew 12 28|Mat.12:28]], [[luke 11 20|Luk.11:20]], [[1-thessalonians 2 16|1Th.2:16]] (cf. προ-φθάνω).† (AS)

φθαρτός, -ή, -όν (φθείρω) [in LXX: [[leviticus 22 25|Lev.22:25]] (מִשְׁחָת), [[isaiah 54 17|Isa.54:17]] A א3, Wis.9:15 14:8, 2Ma.7:16 * ;] perishable, corruptible: ἄνθρωπος, [[romans 1 23|Rom.1:23]] (opposite to ἄφθαρτος θεός); στέφανος, [[1-corinthians 9 25|1Co.9:25]] (opposite to αρτος); σπσρά, [[1-peter 1 23|1Pe.1:23]] (opposite to ἄφθ.); neut., τὸ φ. τοῦτο, [[1-corinthians 15 53|1Co.15:53-54;]] pl., [[1-peter 1 18|1Pe.1:18.]]† (AS)

φθέγγομαι [in LXX for עָנָה, נָבַע hi., etc. ;] of men or animals, to utter a sound or voice: absol., [[acts 4 18|Act.4:18;]] before ἐν φωνῇ, [[2-peter 2 16|2Pe.2:16;]] with accusative, ὑπέρογκα, [[2-peter 2 18|2Pe.2:18.]]† (AS)

φθείρω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת hi., pi., also for חָבַל, etc. ;] to destroy, corrupt, spoil (on the varied usage and distinctive meaning of the word, see Mayor on 2Pe, App., 175 ff.): with accusative, [[1-corinthians 3 17|1Co.3:17 15:23]], [[2-corinthians 7 2|2Co.7:2]]; before ἀπό, [[2-corinthians 11 3|2Co.11:3;]] ἐν, [[2-peter 2 12|2Pe.2:12]], Ju 10, [[revelation 19 2|Rev.19:2]]; κατά, [[ephesians 4 22|Eph.4:22]] (cf. δια-, κατα-φθείρω).† (AS)

φθιν-οπωρινός, -ή, -όν (φθινόπωρον, late autumn), autumnal: δένδρα φ., autumn trees (said to be without fruit therefore at a time when fruit might be expected; see Mayor's elaborate note, Ep. Ju., 55-59, and reff. there): Ju 12.† (AS)
φθόγγος, -ου, ὁ (φθέγγομαι), [in LXX: [[psalms 19 4|Psa.19:4]] (קַו), Wis.19:18 * ;] a sound: [[romans 10 18|Rom.10:18]] (LXX) [[1-corinthians 14 7|1Co.14:7.]]† (AS)
φθονέω, -ῶ (φθόνος), [in LXX: Tob.4:7, 16 AB * ;] to envy: with dative (L, txt., Tr., mg., WH, mg., accusative), as in cl., [[galatians 5 26|Gal.5:26.]]† (AS)

φθόνος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Wis.2:24 6:23, 1Ma.8:16, 3Ma.6:7 * ;] envy: [[romans 1 29|Rom.1:29]], [[galatians 5 21|Gal.5:21]], [[1-timothy 6 4|1Ti.6:4]], [[titus 3 3|Tit.3:3]], [[1-peter 2 1|1Pe.2:1]]; διὰ φθόνον, [[matthew 27 18|Mat.27:18]], [[mark 15 10|Mrk.15:10]], [[philippians 1 15|Php.1:15]]; πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τ. πνεῦμα (on the meaning, see R, txt., mg. 1, 2; Hort, Ja., 93 f.), [[james 4 5|Jas.4:5.]]† (AS)

φθορά, -ᾶς, ἡ (φθείρω) [in LXX for שַׁחַת, חֶבֶל, etc. ;] destruction, corruption, decay (see Mayor on 2Pe, App.,175 ff.): [[romans 8 21|Rom.8:21]], [[1-corinthians 15 42|1Co.15:42]], [[colossians 2 22|Col.2:22]], [[2-peter 2 12|2Pe.2:12]]; opposite to ζωὴ αἰώνιος, [[galatians 6 8|Gal.6:8;]] by meton., of that which is subject to corruption, [[1-corinthians 15 50|1Co.15:50;]] of moral decay, [[2-peter 1 4|2Pe.1:4 2:12 2:19]] (cf. Wis.14:12).† (AS)
φιάλη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for מִזְרָק ;] a shallow bowl (= Lat. patera), used for pouring libations, etc.: [[revelation 5 8|Rev.5:8 15:7 16:1-17 17:1 21:9]].† (AS)
φιλ-άγαθος, -ον [in LXX: Wis.7:22 * ;] loving that which is good, loving goodness: [[titus 1 8|Tit.1:8]] (Arist., Polyb., a l.).† (AS)
Φιλαδελφία (Rec. -έλφεια), -ας, ἡ Philadelphia, a city of Lydia: [[revelation 1 11|Rev.1:11 3:7]].† (AS)

φιλαδελφία, -ας, ἡ (φιλάδελφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 13:26 4Mac 14:1 * ;] the love of brothers, brotherly love: of Christians' mutual love as brethren (see: ἀδελφός), [[romans 12 10|Rom.12:10]], [[1-thessalonians 4 9|1Th.4:9]], [[hebrews 13 1|Heb.13:1]], [[1-peter 1 22|1Pe.1:22]], [[2-peter 1 7|2Pe.1:7]].† (AS)

φιλ-άδελφος, -ον [in LXX: 2Ma.15:14, 4Ma.13:21 4Mac 15:10 * ;] loving one's brother, loving like a brother (Soph., Xen., al.): of Christians' love for one another (EV, loving as brethren), [[1-peter 3 8|1Pe.3:8.]]† (AS)
φίλανδρος, -ον 1. loving men (Æsch.). 2. Of a wife, loving her husband (frequently in epitaphs, see LS, see word, Deiss., BS, 255): [[titus 2 4|Tit.2:4.]]† (AS)

φιλανθρωπία, -ας, ἡ (φιλάνθρωπος, humane), [in LXX: [[esther 8 13|Est.8:13]], 2Ma.6:22 2Mac 14:9, 3Ma.3:15 3Mac 3:18 * ;] humanity, kindness (see Field, Notes, 147 f.): [[acts 28 2|Act.28:2]], [[titus 3 4|Tit.3:4]] (cf. also DCG, ii, 356 ff.).† (AS)
φιλανθρώπως adv., [in LXX: 2Ma.9:27, 3Ma.3:20 * ;] humanely, kindly: [[acts 27 3|Act.27:3.]]† (AS)
φιλαργυρία, -ας, ἡ (φιλάργυρος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 2:15 א1 * ;] love of money, avarice: [[1-timothy 6 1|1Ti.6:1.]]† SYN.: πλεονεξία, covetousness (see Tr., Syn., § xxiv) (AS)
φιλ-άργυρος, -ον [in LXX: 4Ma.2:8 * ;] loving money, avaricious: [[luke 16 14|Luk.16:14]], [[2-timothy 3 2|2Ti.3:2]].† (AS)
φίλ-αυτος, -ον loving oneself (Arist.); in bad sense (ib.), selfish: [[2-timothy 3 2|2Ti.3:2.]]† SYN.: αὐθάδης (see Tr., Syn., § xciii) (AS)

φιλέω, -ῶ (φίλος), [in LXX: [[genesis 27 4|Gen.27:4]], 9, al. (אָהַב), [[genesis 27 27|Gen.27:27]], al. (נָשַׁק), [[lamentations 1 2|La 1:2]] (רֵעַ) Wis.8:2, al. ;] 1. to love (with the love of emotion and friendship, Lat, amare; v, SYN.): with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 10 37|Mat.10:37]], [[john 5 20|Jhn.5:20]]; [[john 11 3|Jhn.11:3, 36 15:19 16:27 20:2 21:15-17]], [[1-corinthians 16 22|1Co.16:22]], [[revelation 3 19|Rev.3:19]]; ἐν πίστει, [[titus 3 15|Tit.3:15;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 23 6|Mat.23:6]], [[luke 20 46|Luk.20:46]], [[john 12 25|Jhn.12:25]], [[revelation 22 15|Rev.22:15]]; with inf. ([[isaiah 56 10|Isa.56:10;]] cf. Bl., § 69, 4), [[matthew 6 5|Mat.6:5.]] 2. to kiss: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 26 48|Mat.26:48]], [[mark 14 44|Mrk.14:44]], [[luke 22 47|Luk.22:47]] (cf. κατα-φιλέω).† SYN.: ἀγαπάω ω (which see), the love of duty and respect (AS)
φιλήδονος, -ον (φίλος, ἡδονή), loving pleasure: [[2-timothy 3 4|2Ti.3:4]] (Polyb., Plut. al.).† (AS)

φίλημα, -τος, τό (φιλέω), [in LXX: [[proverbs 27 6|Pro.27:6]], [[song-of-solomon 1 2|Sng.1:2]] (נְשִׁיקָה) * ;] a kiss: [[luke 7 45|Luk.7:45 22:48]]; as a token of Christian brotherhood, φ. ἅγιον, [[romans 16 16|Rom.16:16]], [[1-corinthians 16 20|1Co.16:20]], [[2-corinthians 13 12|2Co.13:12]], [[1-thessalonians 5 26|1Th.5:26]]; φ. ἀγάπης, [[1-peter 5 14|1Pe.5:14]] (see Lft., Notes, 90; DB, DCA, see word "Kiss").† (AS)
φιλήμων, -ονος, ὁ Philemon: Phm 1.† (AS)
φίλητός (T, Φιλητός), -ου, ὁ Philetus: [[2-timothy 2 17|2Ti.2:17.]]† (AS)
φιλία, -ας, ἡ (φίλος), [in LXX chiefly for אַהֲבָה ;] friendship: with genitive obj., [[james 4 4|Jas.4:4.]]† (AS)
φιλιππήσιος, -ου, ὁ (for other forms in use, see Lft., in l) a Philippian: [[philippians 4 15|Php.4:15.]]† (AS)
φίλιπποι, -ων, οἱ (on the pl., see WM, § 27, 3) Philippi: [[acts 16 12|Act.16:12 20:6]], [[philippians 1 1|Php.1:1]], [[1-thessalonians 2 2|1Th.2:2]].† (AS)

loving God, pious , (Aristotle Philosopher), etc. (ML)

φιλονεικία, -ας, ἡ (φιλόνεικος), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 8:26 * ;] love of strife, rivalry, emulation (Plat., al.), but mostly in bad sense (Thuc., al.), contentiousness, contention: [[luke 22 24|Luk.22:24]] (but see Field, Notes, 75 f.).† (AS)
φιλό-νεικος, -ον (νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: [[ezekiel 3 7|Eze.3:7]] (חָזָק ־מֵצַח)* ;] fond of strife, contentious: [[1-corinthians 11 16|1Co.11:16.]]† (AS)
φιλο-ξενία, -ας, ἡ (φιλόξενος), love of strangers, hospitality: [[romans 12 13|Rom.12:13]], [[hebrews 13 2|Heb.13:2]].† (AS)
φιλό-ξενος, -ον loving strangers, hospitable: [[1-timothy 3 2|1Ti.3:2]], [[titus 1 8|Tit.1:8]], [[1-peter 4 9|1Pe.4:9]].† (AS)
φιλο-πρωτιύω (φιλόπρωτος, Plut., al.) to strive to be first: III Jn 9 (eccl.).† (AS)

φίλος, -η, -ον [in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ, אָהַב ;] 1. pass., beloved, dear (Hom., Eur., al.). 2. Act., loving, friendly (in cl. less frequently and only in poets): [[acts 19 31|Act.19:31.]] As subst., a friend; (a) masc., ὁ φ.: [[luke 7 6|Luk.7:6 11:5 14:10 15:6 16:9 21:16 23:12]], [[acts 27 3|Act.27:3]], 3Jn.14; opposite to δοῦλος, [[john 15 15|Jhn.15:15;]] φ. ἀναγκαῖοι, [[acts 10 24|Act.10:24;]] with genitive subj., [[matthew 11 19|Mat.11:19]], [[luke 7 34|Luk.7:34 11:6, 8 12:4 14:12 15:29]], [[john 11 11|Jhn.11:11 15:13-14]]; ὁ φ. τοῦ νυμφίου, [[john 3 29|Jhn.3:29;]] τ. Φιλο-σοφία, -ας, ἡ (φιλόσοφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:1 4Mac 5:10 4Mac 5:22 4Mac 7:9 4Mac 7:21 * ;] the love and pursuit of wisdom; hence, philosophy, investi­gation of truth and nature: of the so-called philosophy of false teachers, [[colossians 2 8|Col.2:8]] (see Lft., ICC, in l).† (AS)
φιλό-σοφος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Dan LXX 1:20 (אַשָּׁף), 4Ma.1:1 4Mac 5:35 4Mac 7:7 * ;] a philosopher: [[acts 17 18|Act.17:18.]]† (AS)
φιλόστοργος, -ον (στοργή, family affection), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:13 * ;] tenderly loving, affectionate (Xen., Plut., al.): of Christians, [[romans 12 10|Rom.12:10.]]† (AS)
φιλότεκνος, -ον (φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:4-6 * ;] loving one's children (Hdt., Arist., Plut., al.): of women, joined with φίλανδρος, which see, [[titus 2 4|Tit.2:4.]]† (AS)

φιλοτιμέομαι, -οῦμαι (φίλος, τιμή), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:35 A ;] to love or seek after honour, hence, to be ambitious, emulous (Plat., Plut., al.): with inf., [[romans 15 20|Rom.15:20]], [[2-corinthians 5 9|2Co.5:9]], [[1-thessalonians 4 11|1Th.4:11]].† (AS)
φιλοφρόνως (φιλόφρων) adv., [in LXX: 2Ma.3:9, 4Ma.8:5 * ;] kindly, with friendliness: [[acts 28 7|Act.28:7.]]† (AS)
φιλόφρων, -ον (φίλος, φρήν), friendly, kind. [[1-peter 3 8|1Pe.3:8]], Rec.† (AS)

φιμόω, -ῶ (φιμός, a muzzle), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 25 4|Deu.25:4]] (חָסַם), Dan LXX Su 1:61, 4Ma.1:35 א R * ;] to muzzle: [[1-corinthians 9 9|1Co.9:9]], [[1-timothy 5 18|1Ti.5:18]]" (LXX) ; metaphorically, to put to silence: with accusative of person(s), [[matthew 22 34|Mat.22:34]], [[1-peter 2 15|1Pe.2:15]]; pass., to be silenced, silent: [[matthew 22 12|Mat.22:12]], [[mark 1 25|Mrk.1:25 4:39]], [[luke 4 35|Luk.4:35]].† (AS)
φλέγων, -οντος, ὁ Phlegon: [[romans 16 14|Rom.16:14.]]† (AS)

φλογίζω (φλόξ), [in LXX: [[exodus 9 24|Exo.9:24]] (לָקַח hith.), [[numbers 21 14|Num.21:14]] (†), [[psalms 97 3|Psa.97:3]] (לָהַט pi.), Da TH [[daniel 3 27|Dan.3:27]](94) (חָרַךְ ithp.), Sir.3:30, 1Ma.3:5 * ;] to set on fire, burn, burn up: figuratively, [[james 3 6|Jas.3:6]] (on the meaning of the sentence, see Hort, in l).† (AS)

φλόξ genitive, φλογός, [in LXX chiefly for לַהַב, לֶהָבָה ;] a flame: [[luke 16 24|Luk.16:24;]] φ, πυρός, [[acts 7 30|Act.7:30]], [[2-thessalonians 1 8|2Th.1:8]], [[hebrews 1 7|Heb.1:7]]" (LXX), [[revelation 1 14|Rev.1:14 2:18 19:12]].† (AS)
φλυαρέω, -ῶ (φλύαρος), to talk nonsense: with accusative of person(s), ἡμᾶς (EV, prating against us), III Jn 10.† (AS)
φλύαρος, -ον (φλύω, to babble), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:10 * ;] babbling, garrulous: [[1-timothy 5 13|1Ti.5:13]] (EV, tattlers; of things, φιλοσοφία, 4Mac, l.with).† (AS)

φοβερός, -ά, -όν (φοβέω), [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵא, also for דְּחַל, אָיֹם ;] fearful, whether act, or pass.; 1. act., = δεινός, causing fear, terrible (LXX): [[hebrews 10 27|Heb.10:27, 31 12:21]] 2. Pass., = δειλός, feeling fear, timid (cl. in both senses).† (AS)
